blueprint_concepts: Sum of products of binomial coefficients (sum of C_r.C_(r+k))
english: For each integer $k$ with $0\le k\le10$, let $T_{k}=\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{10-k}(-1)^{r}\binom{10}{r}\binom{10}{r+k}$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{10}T_{k}$ is equal to
hindi: प्रत्येक पूर्णांक $k$, $0\le k\le10$, के लिए माना $T_{k}=\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{10-k}(-1)^{r}\binom{10}{r}\binom{10}{r+k}$ है। तब $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{10}T_{k}$ बराबर है
solution: Partial alternating sum: $\sum_{j=0}^{p}(-1)^{j}\binom{n}{j}=(-1)^{p}\binom{n-1}{p}$ (telescoping by Pascal's rule) $\Rightarrow(-1)^{5}\binom{9}{5}=-126$
solution_full: Write $\binom{10}{r+k}=\binom{10}{10-k-r}$. Then $T_{k}=\sum_{r}(-1)^{r}\binom{10}{r}\binom{10}{(10-k)-r}$, which is the coefficient of $x^{10-k}$ in the product of $(1-x)^{10}=\sum(-1)^{r}\binom{10}{r}x^{r}$ and $(1+x)^{10}=\sum\binom{10}{s}x^{s}$.
Hence $T_{k}=0$ when $10-k$ is odd, and $T_{k}=(-1)^{j}\binom{10}{j}$ when $10-k=2j$. As $k$ runs over $0,\dots,10$, $10-k$ runs over $0,\dots,10$, so the even values give $j=0,1,\dots,5$.
Using $\binom{n}{j}=\binom{n-1}{j}+\binom{n-1}{j-1}$ the partial alternating sum telescopes: $\sum_{j=0}^{p}(-1)^{j}\binom{n}{j}=(-1)^{p}\binom{n-1}{p}$.
(Summing over all coefficients of $(1-x^{2})^{10}$ instead, i.e. putting $x=1$, would give $0$, option (C).)
originality_note: New: a family of alternating product sums T_k is summed over the shift k, so only the coefficients of x^0..x^10 of (1-x^2)^10 survive and a partial alternating sum appears (way 5). Closest known: sum (-1)^r C_r^2 or sum C_r C_(r+k). Different because: the outer sum over k reduces to half of the coefficients, which needs the partial alternating-sum identity.

concept_use.Binomial sums with alternating signs: T_k comes from (1-x)^10 and the final step is the partial alternating sum sum_{j<=5} (-1)^j C(10,j) = -C(9,5).
concept_use.Sum of products of binomial coefficients: Each T_k is a sum of products C(10,r) C(10,r+k), evaluated as a coefficient of (1-x)^10 (1+x)^10.

stem_review: Read as a student: k range and summation range for r stated, T_k defined for every k; answer -126 at option A as planned; options numbers; Hindi mirrors. No change.
key_step: Recognise T_k as a coefficient of (1-x^2)^10 and then evaluate a partial alternating sum.
justification: Two linked ideas (product-of-coefficients as a coefficient of a product, then the partial alternating sum); neither is hard alone, but the student must combine them. Comparable to the L3 two-step anchors such as 2026-P1-Q11 (L3).
